factors.name: Solar ITC forfeiture absent documented physical-work BOC by Jul 4, 2026 — ~$45.6M face los
factors.evidence: Deadline has passed. Under OBBBA §70512 amending IRC §48E, solar facilities not beginning construction by Jul 4, 2026 (or PIS by Dec 31, 2027) receive $0. Notice 2025-42 eliminated the 5% safe harbor for >1.5 MWac — only documented physical work of a significant nature counts. On $202M capex with ~$152M solar basis, the lost credit is ~$45.6M face (~$0.25/Wac, 22.5% of capex), requiring +$3–5/MWh PPA uplift to hold returns. Post-deadline options: (1) storage-only ITC under §48E (storage exempt from the cliff; 30% through 2033, phase-down 2034–35); (2) transferability of the surviving storage credit under §6418; (3) domestic-content/energy-community adders on the storage tranche only. None restore the solar credit.
sources: KB: RAI Solar A financials — ITC cliff kill-variable

factors.name: Storage-only ITC fallback requires basis segregation and FEOC-compliant BESS supply chain
factors.evidence: The surviving credit attaches only to energy storage technology basis. KB project split implies ~$50M BESS basis → ~$15M ITC; market turnkey for 320 MWh at $200–350/kWh implies $64–112M basis → $19–34M. The $202M/180 MWac = $1.12/Wac figure is PV-only scope — if the 80/320 BESS is inside $202M the project is $40–70M short and the ITC basis split is wrong. Separately, OBBBA's material-assistance cost ratio (Notice 2026-15) zeroes even the storage credit if cells/modules come from prohibited foreign entities (CATL/BYD effectively excluded), constraining integrator selection and cost.

findings.title: Solar ITC forfeiture absent documented physical-work BOC by Jul 4, 2026 — ~$45.6M face los
findings.text: Deadline has passed. Under OBBBA §70512 amending IRC §48E, solar facilities not beginning construction by Jul 4, 2026 (or PIS by Dec 31, 2027) receive $0. Notice 2025-42 eliminated the 5% safe harbor for >1.5 MWac — only documented physical work of a significant nature counts. On $202M capex with ~$152M solar basis, the lost credit is ~$45.6M face (~$0.25/Wac, 22.5% of capex), requiring +$3–5/MWh PPA uplift to hold returns. Post-deadline options: (1) storage-only ITC under §48E (storage exempt from the cliff; 30% through 2033, phase-down 2034–35); (2) transferability of the surviving storage credit under §6418; (3) domestic-content/energy-community adders on the storage tranche only. None restore the solar credit.

findings.title: Storage-only ITC fallback requires basis segregation and FEOC-compliant BESS supply chain
findings.text: The surviving credit attaches only to energy storage technology basis. KB project split implies ~$50M BESS basis → ~$15M ITC; market turnkey for 320 MWh at $200–350/kWh implies $64–112M basis → $19–34M. The $202M/180 MWac = $1.12/Wac figure is PV-only scope — if the 80/320 BESS is inside $202M the project is $40–70M short and the ITC basis split is wrong. Separately, OBBBA's material-assistance cost ratio (Notice 2026-15) zeroes even the storage credit if cells/modules come from prohibited foreign entities (CATL/BYD effectively excluded), constraining integrator selection and cost.

findings.title: Transferability monetization haircut and compliance costs on surviving credits
findings.text: §6418 transferability survived OBBBA and is the monetization path absent tax-equity appetite, but credits clear at $0.88–$0.94 per $1.00. On the full $60.6M grandfathered credit that is a $3.6–7.3M discount plus 1.5–3% for transfer insurance/indemnity; on the storage-only fallback ($15–34M) the discount is $0.9–4.1M. Transfers are one-time, cash-only, post-PIS elections, and transferees cannot be specified foreign entities — buyer diligence and recapture indemnities (5-year ITC recapture period) must be priced into the model.

findings.title: Continuity safe harbor leaves thin schedule margin to the Dec 31, 2030 PIS backstop
findings.text: Even with a valid 2026 BOC, the continuity safe harbor requires PIS by Dec 31, 2030. Q4 2029 COD fits with ~12 months cushion, but the KB flags interconnection as the second kill-variable: cluster study must complete ~mid-2027 and network-upgrade allocation vs the $24M trigger is unresolved; GSU transformer lead times run 128–144 weeks. Slippage past 2030 forfeits even a grandfathered credit; a missed-BOC project has no such protection at all on the solar tranche.
